title: The Nairobi Hospital School of Nursing September 2011 Class GIT Disorders End of Block I Supplementary Examination

sets.title: Set 1: Original Exam Questions
sets.description: The original MCQs and True/False statements from The Nairobi Hospital School of Nursing September 2011 class GIT Disorders End of Block I Supplementary Examination paper (GIT Disorders, sat 26 July 2012, Part A, Q1 to Q10).

questions.explanation: Trypsinogen auto digests the pancreas (A) is correct because in acute pancreatitis the pancreatic enzymes, especially trypsinogen, are prematurely activated to trypsin inside the pancreas itself; trypsin then activates other enzymes (lipase, elastase, phospholipase) and the gland digests itself, causing inflammation, edema, necrosis and hemorrhage. Pain is relieved by antacids (B) is incorrect because the severe epigastric pain radiating to the back is not acid-related; it is relieved by opioid analgesia, nil by mouth and leaning forward with the knees flexed. Bile activates the pancreatic enzymes (C) is incorrect as the best answer: reflux of bile into the pancreatic duct is one proposed trigger, but it is the activation of trypsinogen to trypsin that is the key event. Serum amylase levels are decreased (D) is incorrect because serum amylase and lipase rise (typically more than three times the normal) within hours of the attack. Note: the bile reflux theory makes option C partly plausible, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: Pain following ingestion of food is common in the following conditions:
questions.explanation: Acute pancreatitis, Crohn's disease (B) is correct from the options because eating stimulates the pancreas to secrete enzymes and so brings on or worsens the pain of acute pancreatitis, and in Crohn's disease the passage of food through the inflamed small bowel causes postprandial cramping pain (which makes the patient afraid to eat). Appendicitis, gastroenteritis (A) is incorrect because the pain of appendicitis is not related to meals (the patient is anorexic) and gastroenteritis gives cramps with diarrhoea and vomiting. Diverticular disease, duodenal ulcers (C) is incorrect because the pain of a duodenal ulcer is typically relieved by food and occurs 2 to 3 hours after meals or at night. Intestinal obstruction, gastric ulcers (D) is incorrect as the best answer, although gastric ulcer pain does occur 30 to 60 minutes after eating, the pain of obstruction is colicky and not tied to eating. Note: option D contains one classic postprandial condition (gastric ulcer), so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: D-xylose test is used to assess the following nutrient absorption:
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates (A) is correct because D-xylose is a simple sugar (a pentose) that is absorbed in the small intestine without needing digestion by pancreatic enzymes; after an oral dose the blood and urine levels are measured, and low levels show malabsorption due to disease of the small intestinal mucosa (for example celiac disease, tropical sprue). Fats (B) is incorrect because fat absorption is assessed by the 72-hour fecal fat test. Proteins (C) is incorrect because protein absorption is not tested by D-xylose. Vitamins (D) is incorrect because vitamin B12 absorption is assessed by the Schilling test.

questions.text: The following is a manifestation of constipation:
questions.explanation: Presence of borborygmus sounds (B) is correct because the manifestations of constipation include abdominal distention, borborygmi (rumbling gas sounds from the bowel), pain and pressure, sensation of incomplete evacuation, straining at stool and the passage of small, hard, dry stool. Perianal incontinence (A) is incorrect because it is not a primary feature of constipation (it may only occur as overflow leakage in fecal impaction). Painful spasmodic contractions (C) is incorrect as the best answer because colicky pain is a feature of diarrhoea, obstruction and irritable bowel syndrome, and in constipation the pain is a dull ache and pressure. Increased appetite (D) is incorrect because constipation causes decreased appetite. Note: option C is also plausible, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: The following is a feature of second degree internal hemorrhoids:

options.A: There is no protrusion to external anal sphincter
options.B: They protrude and require manual reduction

questions.explanation: They protrude but reduce spontaneously (C) is correct because second degree internal hemorrhoids prolapse through the anus during defecation or straining and then return on their own when the straining stops. There is no protrusion to external anal sphincter (A) is incorrect because it describes first degree hemorrhoids, which bleed but do not prolapse. They protrude and require manual reduction (B) is incorrect because it describes third degree hemorrhoids. They are irreducibly prolapsed (D) is incorrect because it describes fourth degree hemorrhoids, which stay outside and may become strangulated or thrombosed.

options.C: There is a sense of fullness after eating a small meal
options.D: The stomach is displaced upwards and slides in and out of thorax

questions.explanation: There is a sense of fullness after eating a small meal (C) is correct because in a paraesophageal (rolling) hernia part of the stomach (the fundus and greater curvature) pushes up through the diaphragmatic hiatus beside the esophagus, while the gastroesophageal junction stays in its normal place below the diaphragm; the herniated stomach is compressed, so the patient feels full after a small meal, and may have discomfort or a feeling of chest pressure and breathlessness after eating. Heartburn and dysphagia are common (A) is incorrect because these are the main features of a sliding hernia, in which the sphincter is incompetent, and reflux is uncommon in the rolling type. The gastroesophageal sphincter is displaced (B) is incorrect because the sphincter is displaced above the diaphragm in a sliding hernia. The stomach is displaced upwards and slides in and out of thorax (D) is incorrect because it describes a sliding hernia. Note: a rolling hernia can strangulate, so surgical repair is advised.

questions.text: Palliative treatment in management of cancer of esophagus involves:
questions.explanation: Insertion of prosthetic tube (C) is correct because palliation aims to relieve the dysphagia and keep the lumen open when the cancer cannot be cured, and this is done by placing a prosthetic tube (an esophageal stent) across the tumour, together with other measures such as laser therapy, dilatation, radiotherapy and gastrostomy or jejunostomy feeding. Diet supplementation with Vitamin C (A) is incorrect because it does not relieve the obstruction or treat the tumour. Surgical resection with anastomosis (B) is incorrect because it is a curative treatment, used for early disease. Injection of botulinum toxin (botox) (D) is incorrect because it is used to relax the lower esophageal sphincter in achalasia.

questions.text: In Zollinger Ellison syndrome, there is:
questions.explanation: Hypertrophy of gastric mucosa (A) is correct because Zollinger Ellison syndrome is caused by a gastrin-secreting tumour (gastrinoma) of the pancreas or duodenum; the high gastrin level stimulates the parietal cells to secrete large amounts of acid and causes hypertrophy and hyperplasia of the gastric mucosa, leading to severe, recurrent and often multiple peptic ulcers and diarrhoea. Decreased number of parietal cells (B) is incorrect because the parietal cells increase in number (hyperplasia). Increased insulin production (C) is incorrect because the hormone produced in excess is gastrin and not insulin (an insulinoma causes hypoglycemia). Normal gastric acid secretion (D) is incorrect because the acid secretion is greatly increased.

questions.text: Nursing care following barium study involves:
questions.explanation: Observing for stool characteristics (B) is correct because the barium is passed in the stool and turns it white or pale for 1 to 3 days, so the nurse observes the stool to confirm that the barium has been expelled; the patient is given a laxative or increased fluids to prevent barium impaction and constipation, and the nurse reports if the stool has not changed colour within 2 to 3 days. Administration of antidiarrhoeals (A) is incorrect because barium causes constipation, and not diarrhoea, so laxatives are given. Observe for occult blood (C) is incorrect because barium does not cause bleeding and the nurse is not testing for it. Limiting food and fluid intake (D) is incorrect because the patient is encouraged to take plenty of fluids to help flush out the barium.

questions.text: In Achalasia, there is sensation of food sticking in upper esophagus.
questions.explanation: False (B) is correct because in achalasia the lower esophageal sphincter fails to relax and the esophageal body has lost peristalsis, so the patient feels food sticking in the lower esophagus behind the sternum (substernal); a sensation of food sticking in the upper esophagus or throat suggests oropharyngeal dysphagia or a lesion of the upper esophagus.

questions.text: H. Pylori metabolizes carbon dioxide to release urea.
questions.explanation: False (B) is correct because it is the other way around: H. pylori produces the enzyme urease, which breaks down (metabolizes) urea to release carbon dioxide and ammonia; the ammonia neutralises the stomach acid around the bacterium and so allows it to survive. This is the basis of the urea breath test and the rapid urease (CLO) test.
